title: config.routing: a tenant's routing policy (0.11.0; levers and VIP 0.12.0)
description: One document per tenant on the compacted topic config.routing (key: the tenant_id), published by admin-console; parity-cc-routing reads it (its seed file until then). PLAN §4.3/§4.5 of parity-cc-routing. A document older than the one held, or naming a queue the tenant doesn't have, is refused whole and counted. Pins are separate documents (config.routing_pin).

version.description: Rises with every change; RE keeps the newest

mode.description: off: phase 4's behaviour (configured sets, config weights and delays); advise: the optimizer only recommends (parity.staffing); auto: the levers apply by themselves: (a) each queue's dispatch weight and secondary delay within their bounds, (b) min_agents/max_agents in the dispatch. No mode moves agents between queues automatically (0.12.0); approvals of recommendations become pins

dwell_min_s.description: D_min: an agent stays on a primary at least this long before the optimizer moves it again (default 300)

reject_skip_s.description: How long a reject skips the agent for that call while another eligible agent is ready (default 30)

alpha.description: The optimizer's weight on missed service level (default 1)

min_agents.description: Lever (b), auto mode: while fewer agents than this are busy on the queue (offered, reserved, on a call or in wrap-up), an agent at its next READY takes this queue's call before other normal calls (0.12.0; it was a primaries floor in 0.11.0); 0: none

max_agents.description: Lever (b), auto mode: with this many agents busy on the queue, an agent at its next READY takes its call only when it has no other (it never idles past a delay: the bounded wait stands); 0: no ceiling

secondary_delay_s.description: d_i's default: secondaries take a call after it waited this long (default 10); in auto the optimizer moves it within delay_min_s..delay_max_s

escalate_after_s.description: After this, any eligible agent may take the call (default 3 x the queue's service-level threshold)

weight.description: 0.12.0, lever (a): the queue's dispatch weight w (an agent takes the highest w x age / tau); default 1; in auto the optimizer moves it within weight_min..weight_max

delay_min_s.description: 0.12.0: lever (a)'s lower bound on the secondary delay (default 0)

delay_max_s.description: 0.12.0: lever (a)'s upper bound on the secondary delay (default max(60, secondary_delay_s))

sl_target.description: 0.12.0, lever (c): staffing recommendations ask for agents while the predicted service level is below this (default 0.8)

vip_sla_s.description: 0.12.0: the VIP class's service-level threshold (default: the queue's)

vip_alpha.description: 0.12.0: the optimizer's weight on the VIP class's missed service level (default 2)

vip_beta.description: 0.12.0: the optimizer's weight on the VIP class's abandonment (default 2)

vip_reserved_min.description: 0.12.0: VIP-eligible agents (vip_skill) kept READY for VIP callers: while no more than this many are READY for the queue, its normal calls reach them only past the secondary delay; 0: none

vip_skill.description: 0.12.0: agents holding this skill are VIP-eligible (a queue's vip_reserved_min keeps that many of them READY for VIP callers). Absent: no reserve

proficiency_speed.description: 0.12.0: configured proficiency -> relative speed for the model (an agent's speed on a queue is the last step its level in the queue's skills reaches; never measured per person). Absent: every agent at speed 1
